scientific_question: Does reduced CA1 pyramidal neuron abundance provide a strong donor-level marker of faster memory decline after adjusting for age, Braak stage, CERAD, and sex?
approach: For each donor, load the slide named in training_cohort.csv, assign cell centroids to CA1 polygon(s), and identify cells classified as Pyramidal Neuron. Compute a donor-level CA1 pyramidal abundance score using the tested normalization variant: either pyramidal count divided by all CA1 cells, or pyramidal count divided by annotated CA1 area. If CA1 is missing, has zero area, or has too few assigned cells for a stable estimate, return NaN rather than forcing a value.

variations.name: ca1_pyramidal_fraction
variations.description: Baseline: number of CA1 Pyramidal Neuron cells divided by total classified cells assigned to CA1.

variations.name: ca1_pyramidal_density
variations.description: Nearby normalization change: number of CA1 Pyramidal Neuron cells divided by total annotated CA1 area after polygon scaling.

notes: Use slide_name to open the paired /data/*.svs.zarr store. Region polygons in CustomAnnotations are stored at 16x cell coordinates, so divide polygon coordinates by 16 before centroid-in-polygon tests. If there are multiple CA1 polygons, combine them logically as one region. For the density variant, compute polygon area after scaling to cell-coordinate space; absolute unit conversion is optional because slide MPP varies only slightly, but keep the implementation deterministic. This candidate only needs centroids, classification labels, and region polygons; contour area is not required.
rationale: With an empty panel, the best seed is a canonical, region-specific hippocampal signal that is common enough to be stable across all donors and simple enough to audit from raw annotations. CA1 pyramidal neuron loss is a biologically direct memory-circuit readout, should have high coverage, and gives a clean starting point before later rounds test gliosis or spatial niche refinements around the same vulnerable subfield.
